name: mirage
text: Mostly yes, but the forms alone are not quite enough. Ally (1099-INT, and the 1099-B for Ally Invest) is the easy part: save them and tax software imports them. For Novig, BetMGM and Kalshi, the official form may not exist or may only show part of the picture (BetMGM sends a form only for large single wins; Novig and Kalshi may send nothing or a summary). The IRS still wants your total winnings, so also save each site's full account or transaction history for the year (a CSV download in January). With the forms plus those histories, it is an easy-to-moderate job: roughly 2-4 hours in tax software, plus the NJ/MD part. The two things forms will not settle are (1) whether you are an NJ or Maryland resident, and (2) whether you itemize. A one-time CPA check on those two is the best use of money. Our Tracker can fill in the gambling totals if a site's history is thin. General info only, not tax advice.
